Article Title: Delhi Police claims only 3,000 cops present for 10,000 protesters, file 15 FIRs
Article Text:
Delhi police uses facial recognition system at Jantar Mantar

NEW DELHI: Amid the ongoing student protest, Delhi police have deployed around 3,000 police personnel to maintain law and order for nearly 10,000 people present in and around Jantar Mantar.Police sources said around 130 police personnel have been injured and 15 FIRs have been registered in connection with the agitation, according to Delhi Police sources. The police also said around 65 students sustained injuries during the demonstrations.The Delhi Police further said it is using Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras to identify "anti-social elements" visiting Jantar Mantar.According to police sources, more than 2,000 people with criminal records who had visited the protest site have been identified so far, as cited by ANI.This is not the first time the Delhi Police has deployed Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras.The force has previously used the technology as part of security arrangements during Republic Day, Independence Day, Holi, Diwali, Eid, Ramlila celebrations and several other major public events across the city.Meanwhile, Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday said he has been diagnosed with typhoid but asserted that the nationwide protests demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan would continue without interruption.On Friday, Dipke welcomed activist Sonam Wangchuk's decision to end his 26-day hunger strike but reiterated that the movement would continue until its demand for accountability over the examination irregularities is met."Our demonstration will go on until Dharmendra Pradhan steps down. Any meeting must take place at a neutral location or venue. Nothing less than the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan will be accepted," he said.Meanwhile, activist Sonam Wangchuk responded to criticism over his decision to end his 26-day hunger strike held in support of students protesting the alleged NEET paper leak.In a video message shared on social media, Wangchuk questioned why his commitment to the cause required a "character certificate".Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike after receiving a written assurance from the Union government on the NEET examination issue and broader systemic reforms to the country's competitive examination framework.The activist said he had earlier been offered verbal assurances but insisted on a written commitment, which delayed the end of his fast by two days.Following a nearly two-hour meeting with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, representatives of CJP said the government had sought time until Saturday afternoon to consider their demand for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
Article Summary: Delhi police uses facial recognition system at jantar mantar to identify "anti-social elements" police sources said around 130 police personnel have been injured and 15 firs have been registered. Activist sonam wangchuk responded to criticism over his decision to end his 26-day hunger strike held in support of students protesting the alleged neet paper leak.

Article Title: Govt fact-checks viral AI deepfakes of PM, ministers; points to Pakistani handles
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The government has debunked doctored videos circulating on social media that wrongly showed Prime Minister Narendra Modi making threatening remarks against those protesting at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar over perpetual NEET paper leak. The Press Information Bureau (PIB) fact check unit said the clips were AI-generated deepfakes and did not reflect the Prime Minister’s actual statements.In related fact-checks, the government also flagged manipulated videos of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and commerce minister Piyush Goyal that were circulating on social media, falsely portraying them as making similar remarks against protesting students.In a post on X, the PIB fact check unit said, “Pakistani propaganda accounts are circulating a video of Prime Minister @narendramodi featuring fabricated statements that he never made regarding the protest in Delhi.”It added, “#PIBFactCheck: This is an '#AI-generated deepfake video' shared to mislead the public. Prime Minister Narendra Modi did NOT make any such statement.”The fact-check unit said the original video shared by PM Modi had been digitally altered to create a misleading version.It further shared a link to the original, unedited video posted by the PM.The fake video circulating online showed an altered audio track in which PM Modi was allegedly made to say, "We are warning people against participating in the Cockroach Janata Party protest. Those who defy this warning will face strict action from the Government of India to ensure that such behaviour is not repeated in the future. Students are advised to focus on their education, failing which they will be compelled to face serious consequences. We are issuing a clear warning to the students."The original video, posted by PM on his official social media account on Thursday, has since garnered 334 million views on Instagram. In the video, PM Modi addressed viewers as “Friends” and spoke directly into what appeared to be a phone’s front camera, held at arm’s length, with no podium, studio setup or formal backdrop.In the video, the PM said the paper leak issue had caused difficulties for lakhs of students and their parents. He said those responsible had been arrested and that steps were being taken to ensure students did not lose an academic year.The Prime Minister also said provisions for fast-track courts had been prepared and would be taken up by the Union cabinet.The fact check unit also debunked another AI-generated video that falsely showed the PM similar remarks about the cockroach janata party protests. In this manipulated clip, Modi appeared to say, “What is the problem with these cockroaches? Even if one paper gets leaked, what is the big deal? Students can simply appear for the examination again next year.” The PIB clarified that the remarks were fabricated and shared the original video, which showed the Prime Minister speaking about the monsoon and the ongoing Monsoon session of parliament.Additionally, the PIB flagged another digitally altered video of Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan that falsely portrayed him threatening protesting students. The manipulated clip appeared to show Pradhan saying that “big leaders do not resign because of these cockroaches; they crush them under their shoes and throw them into dirty drains where they belong” and warning that protesters would “soon face grave consequences”. Refuting the claims, the PIB said, “Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan did not make any such statement.”The fact-check unit blamed Pakistani propaganda accounts for circulating the digitally altered video containing fabricated claims. The original video was posted on the occasion of Sital Sasthi and made no reference to the protests.The manipulated clip surfaced amid continuing protests led by the CJP, which has consistently demanded that Pradhan be held accountable for the alleged NEET paper leaks and has called for the education minister's resignation as one of its principal demands.In another fact check, the government flagged a separate manipulated video involving commerce minister Piyush Goyal, which falsely claimed that Goyal had made similar threatening remarks against Jantar Mantar protests.The PIB said, “Mr Goyal has made no such statement regarding the protests.”The government urged people to verify the authenticity of videos and rely on official sources before sharing them.
Article Summary: The press information bureau (pib) fact check unit said the clips were ai-generated deepfakes. In related fact-checks, the government also flagged manipulated videos of education minister dharmendra pradhan and commerce minister piyush goyal. The clips falsely portrayed them as making similar remarks against protesting students.

Article Title: 'Metro, internet shut - but not paper leaks': Rahul Gandhi slams Centre over NEET protest curbs
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Saturday stepped up his attack on the Narendra Modi-led Centre, accusing it of taking "cruel steps" against students protesting over the NEET paper leak issue at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.Referring to the restrictions imposed in the national capital, including the closure of metro stations, roads, internet services and food supplies, Rahul Gandhi alleged that the government was trying to suppress the student movement.In a post on X, he wrote: "Shut down the metro. Shut down the roads. Shut down the shops. Shut down the Internet. Shut down the food.""The government has taken these cruel steps against students who are demanding their rights. But there's just one thing they couldn't shut down, Mr. Modi—paper leaks," Rae Bareli MP added.The Congress leader's remarks come a day after he accused the Centre and the Delhi Police of "barbarity" during the July 20 "Sansad Chalo" march led by the Cockroach Janta Party over alleged paper leaks.Sharing a video of a student who was allegedly injured after being hit by pellets during the protest, Rahul claimed the government had surpassed even the British era in its treatment of students."Sahil was standing with the Tricolour in his hand, merely asking for a clean, fair exam and the fruit of his hard work--the police raised a gun and badly injured him by firing pellets. This is not British tyranny; it is the barbarity of the Modi government in independent India--where innocent students demanding their rights receive pellets instead of justice," he wrote on X.The July 20 march to Parliament turned violent, leaving more than 118 police personnel injured, including senior officers such as the Special Commissioner, Joint Commissioner, Additional Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, Additional Deputy Commissioner and Assistant Commissioner of Police. Several women police personnel were also injured. Around 60 protesters were also reported injured during the clashes.
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi steps up his attack on the narendra modi-led centre. He accuses it of taking "cruel steps" against students protesting over neet paper leak issue. The congress leader's remarks come a day after he accused the centre and the delhi police of "barbarity"

Article Title: 'Barbarity of Modi govt': Rahul Gandhi attacks Centre over July 20 protest crackdown
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi attacks Modi govt over 'brutality' during July 20 student protest

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Saturday criticised the PM Modi-led Centre and the Delhi police over what he called the "brutality" during the July 20 student protests in Delhi.He said that in today's India, students protesting for their rights are getting "pellets" instead of "justice".In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi shared a video of a youth who was allegedly injured after being hit by pellets fired by the Delhi Police during the protest against paper leaks."Sahil was standing with the Tricolour in his hand, merely asking for a clean, fair exam and the fruit of his hard work--the police raised a gun and badly injured him by firing pellets. This is not British tyranny; it is the barbarity of the Modi government in independent India--where innocent students demanding their rights receive pellets instead of justice," the post read.The protesters march to Parliament turned violent, leaving more than 118 police personnel injured, including senior officers such as the Special Commissioner, Joint Commissioner, Additional Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, Additional Deputy Commissioner and Assistant Commissioner of Police.Several women police personnel were also injured. Around 60 protesters were reportedly hurt during the clashes.Meanwhile, on Friday, the Union Cabinet approved amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, to further strengthen the anti-paper leak law amid the continuing nationwide protests over the NEET-UG issue. Sources told news agency ANI the amendment Bill is likely to be introduced in Parliament on Monday, July 27.The decision came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in a late-night video message on X, promised "stricter" action against paper leaks as protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party continued. He also announced that the Union Cabinet would take up a draft Bill.Social activist Sonam Wangchuk has also ended his 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital in the presence of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh after receiving a written assurance from the Union government on the NEET issue and broader reforms in the country's competitive examination system
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi attacks modi govt over 'brutality' during july 20 student protest. He said that in today's india, students protesting for their rights are getting "pellets" instead of "justice" the protesters march to parliament turned violent, leaving more than 118 police personnel injured.

Article Title: 'Rewarding corruption': CJP attacks Centre over education secretary's replacement
Article Text:
Education secretary's transfer triggers fresh CJP attack on Centre

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday alleged that the transfer of the Education Secretary amounted to "rewarding corruption instead of ensuring accountability". He claimed that the official had been replaced by an IAS officer from the Animal Husbandry Department who faces "severe multi-crore corruption charges"."Last night, the Education Secretary was transferred. He was replaced by an IAS officer from the Animal Husbandry Department who has severe multi-crore corruption charges against him. The entire crisis around paper leaks and NEET was about systemic corruption," Dipke said in a post on X.Abhijeet further said that replacing one bureaucrat with another facing "serious corruption allegations" was "a direct insult to young people across India".Questioning whether this was the "compromise" the government expected students to accept, he asserted that "this is not accountability" and said the protest would continue until Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns."Replacing one bureaucrat with another facing serious corruption allegations is a direct INSULT to young people across India.Is this the "compromise" the government expects us to accept? This is not accountability. We will not stop until Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns," Dipke added.The Centre on Thursday carried out a major bureaucratic reshuffle, making 13 secretary-level appointments across ministries and departments, including key changes in the education ministry, amid continuing protests over the alleged NEET paper leak.Senior IAS officer Naresh Pal Gangwar has been appointed Secretary, Department of Higher Education, while T K Anil Kumar has been named Secretary, Department of School Education and Literacy. According to an order issued by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), Gangwar, a 1994-batch IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre, will succeed Vineet Joshi as Secretary of the Department of Higher Education.The agitation over the NEET paper leak spread across several states on Friday, a day after CJP called for nationwide demonstrations. Protesters condemned the Delhi Police crackdown on July 20 and reiterated their demand for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.As the protests gathered momentum across states, the Congress directed its state units to organise candlelight marches and 'satyagraha' in every district on Saturday evening to protest against the "irregularities in the NEET and CBSE examinations and the subsequent repressive actions by the Modi government".On Friday, a high-level meeting between leaders of CJP and senior BJP leaders, including Union Health Minister JP Nadda and Union Minister Jitendra Singh, was held at the Constitution Club in New Delhi.Earlier, activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital in the presence Nadda and Jitendra Singh after the Union government gave a written assurance on the NEET examination issue and broader systemic reforms to the country's competitive examination framework.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi assured that strict action would be taken against those responsible for the alleged paper leaks. He also said the Union Cabinet would consider a draft Bill proposing fast-track courts and stricter punishment for offenders.
Article Summary: Education secretary's transfer triggers fresh cjp attack on centre. Cockroach janata party (cjp) founder abhijeet dipke on saturday alleged that the transfer of the education secretary amounted to "rewarding corruption instead of ensuring accountability" he claimed that the official had been replaced by an ias officer from the animal husbandry department who faces "severe multi-crore corruption charges"

Results will be seen soon, and it will lead to bringing down the cost of electricity," he said at the Adani Presents Times Network Sustainability Conclave 2026.Joshi also pointed to the country's first hydrogen-powered train, saying it places India among a select group of nations investing in the future of sustainable transportation.At the event, MP CM Mohan Yadav elaborated on the state's sustainability initiatives, including efforts towards afforestation and water conservation. Article Title: Treat digital arrests and cyber frauds as organised crime: SC
Article Text:
‘Invoke Stringent Laws To Curb Such Crimes’

NEW DELHI: Maintaining its zero-tolerance approach towards digital arrest and cyber fraud cases, SC Friday said police must invoke charges under stringent laws to prevent such organised crimes.Rejecting the bail plea of Mohamad, aka MD, accused in a case relating to digital arrest followed by fraudsters posing as policemen and showing forged SC orders to coerce a man to part with Rs 76 lakh last year, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, "Digital arrest and cyber fraud cases must be equated with robbery and dacoity. Why are these offences not classified as organised crime?" It asked Gujarat police why they had not added charges under Gujarat Control of Terrorism and Organised Crime Act, which came into force in 2019.When the petitioner's counsel Aastha Mehta said the accused had been in custody for more than a year, and he be granted bail as investigation in the case had been completed, the bench said, "If you want the court to entertain the plea, then the first thing we will do is to add graver charges under the law on organised crime."It was alleged that unknown persons impersonating Mumbai policemen accused the complainant of being involved in a money laundering case and placed him under digital arrest for two days through continuous video calls, during which they forwarded him forged documents purporting to be arrest warrants and judicial orders issued by SC through WhatsApp.SC had taken cognisance of rising digital arrest scams, mostly targeting senior citizens, and asked CBI to probe cases pan-India, and was instrumental in activating an inter-departmental mechanism involving different agencies to implement steps to curb this menace.
Article Summary: ‘invoke stringent laws to curb such crimes’ says supreme court of india. ‘digital arrest and cyber fraud cases must be equated with robbery and dacoity. Why are these offences not classified as organised crime?"

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) on Friday announced that 17 metro stations across the national capital will remain closed for entry and exit from 7.30am on Friday until further instructions, citing "security reasons".The latest advisory marks the third consecutive day of metro disruptions in central Delhi amid the ongoing Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest at Jantar Mantar.In a post on X, the DMRC said interchange facilities will remain available at Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House and Central Secretariat despite the closures.The decision comes a day after the DMRC shut 17 stations on Thursday, following the closure of 16 stations on Wednesday, when hundreds of office-goers, students and other commuters were stranded during the morning rush hour.Entry gates at Mandi House, Rajiv Chowk and Central Secretariat were reopened later on Thursday night.The repeated closures come amid heightened security across central Delhi following the July 20 'Sansad Chalo' march, which witnessed clashes between protesters and police near Parliament.Since then, authorities have maintained heavy security deployment around Jantar Mantar, Parliament and adjoining areas, with prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) remaining in force across the New Delhi district.The CJP has continued its sit-in at Jantar Mantar, demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET paper leak and broader reforms in the examination system.The DMRC has advised commuters to plan their journeys accordingly, adding that normal operations at the affected stations will resume only after further instructions.
Article Summary: 17 delhi metro stations will be closed for entry and exit from friday morning. The latest advisory marks the third consecutive day of metro disruptions in central delhi. The closures come amid heightened security across central delhi following the july 20 'sansad chalo' march.

Article Title: 3 years on, SIT probe complete in just 10% of Manipur riot cases
Article Text: NEW DELHI: More than three years after Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives, Supreme Court was informed Friday that probes into only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by SITs of state police while CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.Appearing for the CBI, additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the central probe agency had filed chargesheets in 21 cases and closure reports in six, of which three had been accepted. It was continuing investigations into the remaining four cases.Former Maharashtra DGP Dattatray Padsalgikar, who was appointed to oversee the investigations, informed the court through a report that of the 3,020 cases being probed by the SITs across eight districts, chargesheets had been filed in only 301 cases and trial had commenced in 10.The CJI-led bench told the investigators to act expeditiously. Given the volume of cases, SC mulled setting up special courts to try these exclusively. It sought responses to this from Manipur govt and the high courts of Assam and Manipur.SC had transferred investigations into cases of rape-murder other heinous offence to CBI and shifted their trial to Guwahati. The central agency told the court that examination of witnesses residing in Manipur through video-conferencing was a challenge because of law-and-order situations, non-cooperation and language barriers as they spoke different dialects.Senior advocate Ngangom Junior Luwang complained that no effort had been made to trace 30 missing people and without their remains, authorities were not issuing death certificates required for other purposes. SC asked him to approach Manipur high court.Advocate Sharukh Alam submitted that land belonging to churches vandalised during the clashes were getting encroached upon and said govt had taken no steps to reconstruct them. Bhati said govt's priority was to reconstruct damaged dwelling units. The bench said govt was right to prioritise reconstructing houses but asked it to take steps to stop encroachment of places of worship.
Article Summary: Only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by sits of state police. Cbi had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it. The cji-led bench told the investigators to act expeditiously.

Article Title: Students protest: Breakthrough with Sonam Wangchuk may help government tackle crisis
Article Text:
Sonam Wangchuk when he broke his hunger strike

NEW DELHI: Government is keeping its fingers crossed after its successful attempt to persuade activist Sonam Wangchuk - whose wide recognition helped expand the reach of Cockroach Janta Party's protest into uncomfortable territory for BJP - to break his hunger strike.CJP's assertion, though, to continue and even escalate the agitation if its demand for education minister Dharmendra Pradhan 's resignation is not met has muddied the waters, but govt feels the successful engagement with the Ladakh activist coupled with measures taken by it will help counter the allegation that govt has not been sensitive to students' concerns and resonate with those not affiliated with AAP, the Left and other opponents and their student outfits.The breakthrough with Wangchuk became possible because of deft footwork, including behind-the-scenes moves by home minister Amit Shah, that saw ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh overcoming the activist and bringing in local netas of Ladakh. Wangchuk's fears about violence and the risk of protests being overtaken - something that he articulated in the video-graphed conversation with the ministers - were helpful.Official circles are hopeful that Wangchuk's appeal for peaceful protests and against any form of violence, besides govt's positive response to his demand for not registering criminal cases against peaceful protestors and suitable compensation to families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide, will have a positive impact and may also help isolate "genuine" students from activists motivated by a dizzying array of motives - from partisan political considerations and gender fluidity to angst over Brahmanical patriarchy and Manuvad and Hindutva dominance.Unlike Abhijeet Dipke-led CJP, Wangchuk has not insisted on Pradhan's resignation. Considering it as the hook that connected that segment of youth with the protest who are not overtly political and might have been even otherwise sympathetic to some of the causes of the party, Wangchuk nuancing his pitch for accountability for paper leaks and expanding it beyond the individual to the ministry should help a govt pitted against a determined and competitive push for the minister's scalp.PM Modi was quick on X to wish the Ladakh activist - who was detained under NSA last year for his alleged role in violent protest in the UT - and that he regains the weight he lost in the fast.CJP could not have been pleased with the turn of events, but it was careful not to express its annoyance. Dipke lauded Wangchuk's "extraordinary courage" but left no doubt that he would carry on with his protest until Pradhan was sacked.The rift was evident after Wangchuk's wife Gitanjali Angmo wrote on X, "Before you rush to criticise Wangchuk, first pause to earn the ethos of fasting for 26 days for a cause larger than yourself. He lies in the ICU today, having lost 11 kg, including muscle mass, because he chose sacrifice over comfort... The least we can offer him is a day of compassion before burdening him with our own expectations and political calculations. Not everyone is qualified to judge a life of selfless service. One must first earn the moral stature to do so. Please. Have a heart."Also read: CJP-Centre 3rd round of talks today; PM Modi, Wangchuk release late night video - top developments BJP's Amit Malviya was quick to take a jibe at Dipke, saying there is now little justification for "his gang" to continue the protest and alleged their objective no longer appears to address students' concerns but to manufacture a political victory by insisting on Pradhan's resignation. It was Wangchuk's forcible removal, although with court authorisation from the protest site on July 18 that imparted the first real burst of agitational energy into the campaign, before the protestors' march to Parliament and police's alleged heavy-handedness turned it into a national headline.Since he broke his 26-day fast by accepting soup from health minister Nadda and without the presence of any CJP representative, telltale signs of the organisation's drift from its star draw have emerged. While doubts persist in govt circles over CJP's motives and its insistence on Pradhan's resignation remains a hurdle, govt will not like to give an impression of sacrificing its key figure to street protests but believes that continuing negotiations with the organisation is an enterprise worth its pursuit. Accused of being tone-deaf over the issue of paper leaks and even insensitive to the growing concerns of candidates of competitive exams, govt believes its engagement with and even concessions to CJP's demands, except Pradhan's ouster, will negate the perception.Dipke's own background with AAP and active support he had received from Left organisations mean that a chunk of agitators is unlikely to back down till govt fully concedes. But govt is keen to bridge its gap with a large chunk of apolitical protestors, who have connected with the concerns being espoused by CJP. Modi has taken the lead by announcing fast-track courts to pursue paper leak cases and a bill to make punishment for the guilty stiffer. Termination of 47 officials of NTA, which holds exams like NEET and JEE, and expected reform measures in education are part of that push.
Article Summary: Government is keeping its fingers crossed after its successful attempt to persuade activist sonam wangchuk to break his hunger strike. Cjp's assertion, though, to continue and even escalate the agitation if its demand for education minister dharmendra pradhan's resignation is not met has muddied the waters.

Article Title: Students' stir: CJP-Centre 3rd round of talks today; PM Modi, Wangchuk release late night videos - top developments
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and activist Sonam Wangchuk. The two shared video messages on social media.

Here are the top developments:

'Your love and trust gave me strength': PM Modi shares new video

After 26 days of hunger, do I need to prove my sincerity?': Sonam Wangchuk

NTA sacks 47 officials, recruitment overhaul begins

Second round of talks ends without breakthrough

Centre seeks more time on Pradhan's resignation

Rahul Gandhi reiterates students' demands

Cabinet approves tougher anti-paper leak law

Supreme Court to hear police action pleas; CJI clarifies earlier remarks

PM Modi promises stricter action

NEW DELHI: The stand-off between the Centre and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over the alleged NEET paper leak continued on Friday, with no breakthrough on the protesters' key demand for the resignation of union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.While the government sought more time to respond after the second round of talks, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi renewed his attack on the Centre, reiterated the students' demands and accused the government of using force against peaceful protesters.Meanwhile, the National Testing Agency (NTA) has terminated the services of 47 officials as part of a major overhaul following the controversy over alleged paper leaks and examination-related irregularities. The move is part of a wider restructuring of the NTA aimed at strengthening accountability and restoring confidence in the examination system.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday shared another video message on social media, thanking people for their support as protests led by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak continued.In the video posted on Instagram, PM Modi said, "Your love and trust gave me strength," while reiterating his commitment to the welfare of students and the government's resolve to act against those responsible for examination irregularities.The latest outreach comes a day after the Prime Minister released an unusual selfie-style video beginning with the words "Hello friends", in which he acknowledged that paper leaks were "not an ordinary matter" and assured students and their families that the government would take stricter action.Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Friday shared an emotional message on social media, questioning why he still had to prove his commitment to the cause.In a post on X, Wangchuk wrote, "AFTER 26 DAYS OF HUNGER DO I NEED TO PROVE MY SINCERITY !!!"The post comes as Wangchuk ended his hunger strike, drawing attention to his demands and sparking reactions on social media.The National Testing Agency (NTA) has terminated 47 officials as part of its biggest overhaul since its formation, with some of those removed also facing legal and criminal action based on internal inquiries and inputs from investigating agencies, government sources said.The agency has also begun rebuilding its workforce by recruiting four General Managers and 16 Young Professionals through the UPSC's PRATIBHA Setu talent pool.The new appointments will focus on cybersecurity, digital forensics, test-centre operations and assessment research, and will be overseen by the K Radhakrishnan-led monitoring committee, which is scheduled to hold its first meeting on July 25.The restructuring follows the alleged NEET-UG paper leak and includes plans to reduce dependence on contractual and outsourced staff, strengthen examination security, review outsourcing practices, and prepare for the shift to computer-based NEET-UG examinations from 2027.Officials said further action and reforms are expected as investigations into examination-related irregularities continue.A CJP delegation held a nearly two-hour meeting with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh at the Constitution Club in New Delhi. The delegation submitted three key demands and a five-point reform charter, but the meeting ended without a final decision.Addressing reporters, Nadda said the government would respond after internal consultations."The meeting went on for almost two hours. They had three main demands and five reform suggestions for exams. We have told them that we will meet them again tomorrow afternoon and tell them about the discussion we had within the government," he said.The next round of talks has been scheduled for Saturday afternoon.CJP leaders said the Centre had sought time till Saturday afternoon to respond to their demand for Pradhan's resignation, which they described as non-negotiable.CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the government had expressed in-principle approval to the other two demands."The government has asked for time till tomorrow afternoon on our demand for Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. We hope the government will remove him soon," he said.CJP leader Saurav Das said the delegation had also sought Rs 1 crore compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide, withdrawal of FIRs and legal cases against protesting students, and a written sovereign guarantee that similar action would not be taken against peaceful protesters in the future. According to the delegation, the government accepted the compensation and FIR-related demands in principle.Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi renewed his demand for Dharmendra Pradhan's removal, alleging that the education minister was responsible for the crisis."Dharmendra Pradhan is a criminal education minister. He has to be removed. He is a symbol of the collapse of our education system. He has to go," Gandhi said.He said students were demanding the removal of the education minister, action against those responsible for the alleged pellet gun use and lathi-charge during the protests, and an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi.During the press conference, Rahul also presented a protester whom he alleged had suffered pellet gun injuries during the Jantar Mantar protest."His eye has suffered damage, and he has lost his vision," Gandhi said, while alleging that the government had falsely denied using pellet guns against protesters.The government has denied using pellet guns during the protest.The union cabinet approved amendments to the Prevention of Paper Leak law, proposing stricter punishment for those involved in examination paper leaks.According to sources, the proposed amendments provide for a maximum jail term of 10 years, a fine of up to Rs 10 crore and an increase in the minimum imprisonment from three years to five years.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government would introduce the Bill in Parliament soon and that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had directed that there should be no delay. Rijiju also criticised the Opposition for disrupting Parliament and urged members to allow a discussion on the issue.The Supreme Court on Friday agreed to hear on July 27 two petitions alleging excessive police action against students protesting over the alleged NEET paper leak.Earlier in the day, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant clarified that reports claiming he had refused to hear a petition on the issue were incorrect."In the last two days, a completely false statement was made that a matter was filed," the CJI said, adding that only a representation had been submitted at that stage and describing the reports as "irresponsible and reckless".A day before the Cabinet decision, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that the government would introduce legislation providing for fast-track courts and stricter punishment in paper leak cases."Paper leaks are not an ordinary matter. For lakhs of students and their parents, it is extremely painful," Modi said.The Prime Minister said the government had ensured that nearly 22 lakh students did not lose an academic year by conducting the examinations again. He also welcomed activist Sonam Wangchuk's decision to end his 26-day hunger strike, while the CJP maintained that its protest would continue until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns.
Article Summary: Prime minister narendra modi and activist sonam wangchuk share video messages on social media. Stand-off between centre and cockroach janta party (cjp) over alleged neet paper leak continues. Second round of talks ends without breakthrough on protesters' key demand for resignation of education minister dharmendra pradhan.

Article Title: NTA sacks 47 officials in rejig, to hire 4 GMs, 16 young professionals
Article Text:
Nationwide protests against paper leaks Temporary hands, P 17 Nationwide protests against paper leaks Temporary hands, P 17 Nationwide protests against paper leaks 1

2

NEW DELHI: National Testing Agency has terminated 47 officials and begun rebuilding its workforce with specialist leadership in cybersecurity, forensic investigation, test-centre operations and assessment research, govt sources said Friday. The crackdown follows the NEET-UG paper leak, which forced nearly 20 lakh candidates to take the medical entrance test again on June 21 after the May 3 exam was cancelled. Some of those terminated will also face legal and criminal action based on internal inquiries and inputs from investigating agencies. More measures are expected as responsibility has been fixed for failures in national entrance exams.The first phase of NTA rebuilding its workforce includes four general manager appointments and 16 young professionals through UPSC's Pratibha Setu portal. The recruitment will be overseen by the K Radhakrishnan-led monitoring committee, which will hold its first meeting Saturday, education ministry sources said. The GMs - who will head different verticals - will be appointed on three-year contracts.Sources said 47 personnel have been terminated, not merely transferred or marked for removal. Their names, ranks and alleged ro-les were not disclosed. Cases indicating criminal wrongdoing will be referred to appropriate agencies, while departmental and legal proceedings will follow separately.The assessment and psychometrics vertical head will oversee question banks, normalisation, equating and calibration, and computer-adaptive testing and AI-assisted assessment. The test-centre operations head will supervise NTA's network across more than 500 cities and select overseas centres, including empanelment, capacity, accessibility, amenities, exam day operations and coordination with administrations.The information security head will serve as chief information security officer, responsible for systems, networks, applications, candidate data, a round-the-clock security operations centre and compliance with data protection, information technology and CERT-In requirements. The vigilance, investigation and forensics head will lead malpractice inquiries, build in-house digital forensics capability and coordinate with CBI, Intelligence Bureau, ED, state police forces and cybercrime units under Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.The Pratibha Setu - Professional Resource and Talent Integration Bridge for Hiring Aspirants - platform gives verified employers access to willing candidates who cleared stages of UPSC exams but were not recommended in the final merit list.Twelve positions will be in academic research, two in legal research and two in finance and accounts. The appointments will be for 24 mo-nths, and extendable to 36 mo-nths based on performance.The changes seek to reduce NTA's dependence on temporary manpower. It has 39 sanctioned permanent posts, all on deputation, but only 24 are filled, against 73 contractual personnel and 124 outsourced workers.Further hiring will follow across 10 functional verticals recommended by the Radhakrishnan committee. NTA has also initiated fresh empanelment of subject experts and translators.The overhaul will accompany changes to exam delivery. NEET-UG will shift from OMR-based testing to computer-based testing from 2027, bringing it closer to JEE Main and CUET. The move should reduce physical movement of papers, enable multiple question sets and create a digital trail, but will require secure centres, stronger cybersecurity and safeguards against technical failures.Govt is also reviewing outsourcing in registration, centre management, technology services and handling of confidential material. The new model will define responsibility, strengthen audits and background checks, reduce agencies handling sensitive information, and impose tougher penalties for security failures.
Article Summary: The crackdown follows the neet-ug paper leak, which forced nearly 20 lakh candidates to take the medical entrance test again on june 21. Some of those terminated will also face legal and criminal action based on internal inquiries and inputs from investigating agencies.

Article Title: SC: Will go the extra mile to fix issues, make NEET foolproof
Article Text:
SC assures Neet will be foolproof

NEW DELHI: Amid street protests by the youth against paper leaks and demands that govt fix accountability and bring reforms, the Supreme Court Friday said the system's ad hocism was "troubling", which could not be allowed to go on and assured that it would "tread an extra mile" to fix the problems and make NEET foolproof.With solicitor general Tushar Mehta contending that govt was ready to tread "10 extra miles" to protect the interests of students and that the matter was being supervised at the highest level, a bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe asked him to expeditiously take a decision. It granted time till Aug 3 to brief them about the contours of the new system.The court also sought the Centre's response on implementing computer-based test for medical entrance on the lines of IIT-JEE. The court was hearing a batch of petitions, including ones filed by the Federation of All India Medical Association and United Doctors Front, seeking the court's intervention to make NEET tamper-free. The SG, at the outset of the hearing, said the issue was under serious consideration of govt and sought adjournment for a few days. He said some developments were likely to take place soon.The bench, however, pointed out various issues which govt needed to address, including implementation of recommendations of the high-level committee headed by former Isro chairman K Radhakrishnan."We will highlight a couple of things we wanted to indicate... Last time, you mentioned the Radhakrishnan committee's recommendations. There is a specific reference to the governing board. So your affidavit should indicate what has been done with respect to the governing board, which would consist of transparency, nominations and stakeholders," the bench said.SC said it will keep monitoring the process till the system is institutionalised. "We are focusing on institutionalisation. Ad-hocism has troubled us the most throughout these years.""A very important aspect is the transition to computer-based testing.... Can it be shifted? How will the data be transferred? How will the data be protected? Data safety is the most important aspect. You indicate to us. Cybersecurity, who is to undertake it, how it is to be conducted etc," the bench asked.Dr Radhakrishnan, head of the monitoring committee constituted by SC in 2024 to suggest ways to strengthen NEET, earlier informed the court the committee had submitted 35 long-term recommendations and around 60 short-term recommendations, most of which had already been implemented. He said the reforms had largely yielded positive results in NEET-PG 2025, which was conducted "mostly satisfactorily" except for some issues such as power outages.
Article Summary: Sc assures neet will be foolproof and says it will "tread an extra mile" to fix the problems. Justices p s narasimha and alok aradhe granted time till aug 3 to brief them about the contours of new system.

Article Title: Fast-track courts in slow lane now, backlog 2.5 lakh cases
Article Text:
Massive backlog in fast-track courts

Justice delayed

NEW DELHI: Fast-track special courts, which are meant to complete trials within a year of taking cognisance of offences related to rape and Pocso Act , have not been working at the expected speed. In 2025, which saw more than 1.4 lakh rape and Pocso cases being registered, only 66,500 were disposed of.The backlog of cases had reached 2.5 lakh on Dec 31, 2025. The trend has been similar over the last three years, with the total pendency at over 2 lakh. Since fast-track special courts were constituted in 2019, case pendency has always been around 2 lakh over the last seven years despite the scheme mandating time-bound trials."The scheme has been extended twice, with the last extension valid up to March 31, 2026, for establishment of 790 fast-track special courts. The scheme has now been extended up to Sept 30 this year," law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal informed Parliament in a written response Thursday.The minister added that according to information made available by high courts, 775 fast-track special courts, including 398 exclusive Pocso (e-Pocso) courts, were functional in 29 states/Union Territories as of April.Centre and states share expenditure on these courts in a 60:40 ratio.This covers the salaries of one judicial officer along with seven support staff for each fast-track court, in addition to a grant for meeting day-to-day expenses.Since the inception of the scheme, Centre has released Rs 1,260 crore to states and UTs to ensure the courts functioned smoothly, Meghwal said.The minister said he had written to chief ministers and Chief Justices of high courts regarding the "need for timely action and strict compliance with timelines under Pocso Act and BNSS".Meghwal, however, said it was the responsibility of states and HCs to recruit judges and fill vacant positions of judicial officers in district and subordinate courts, including fast-track ones.
Article Summary: In 2025, which saw more than 1.4 lakh rape and pocso cases being registered, only 66,500 were disposed of. The trend has been similar over the last three years, with the total pendency at over 2 lakh. Since the inception of the scheme, centre has released rs 1,260 crore to states and uts to ensure the courts functioned smoothly.

Article Title: Ravneet Singh Bittu resigns from Union Council of Ministers; President Murmu accepts resignation
Article Text:
Bittu, a three-time former Congress MP from Punjab, was inducted as a minister of state in the Narendra Modi-led government in June 2024

NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu on Friday accepted the resignation of Union minister of state for railways and food processing industries Ravneet Singh Bittu from the Union Council of Ministers with immediate effect, under Clause (2) of Article 75 of the Constitution of India.Bittu's resignation came after his Rajya Sabha tenure, representing Rajasthan, ended on June 21. He had been a member of the Upper House from August 2024 to June 2026.In a post on X, Bittu wrote, "I express my heartfelt gratitude to Hon’ble President Smt. Droupadi Murmu Ji and Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi Ji for giving me the opportunity to serve the nation as Minister of State in the Government of India. It has been an honour to serve the people of India, especially my beloved Punjab. I remain committed to the ideals of service, nationalism, and the vision of a Viksit Bharat under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji. My journey of public service continues with renewed dedication."A three-time former Congress MP from Punjab, Bittu was inducted as a minister of state in the Narendra Modi-led government in June 2024 despite losing the Lok Sabha election from Ludhiana to Punjab Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring by 20,942 votes.He had joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in March 2024 ahead of the general elections after ending his long association with the Congress. Union Home Minister Amit Shah had projected Bittu as an important Sikh face for the BJP during the election campaign in Punjab.A grandson of former Punjab chief minister Beant Singh, who was assassinated in 1995, Bittu represented Anandpur Sahib in the Lok Sabha in 2009 before winning from Ludhiana in 2014 and 2019. During his political career in the Congress, he also served as the party's leader in the Lok Sabha and as its whip in the Lower House.Bittu's resignation comes as the BJP prepares for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, which the party is expected to contest on its own after ruling out an alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal.The BJP, which won only two seats in the 2022 Punjab Assembly elections, is aiming to improve its performance in the state.
Article Summary: Bittu's resignation came after his rajya sabha tenure, representing rajasthan, ended on june 21. He had been a member of the upper house from august 2024 to june 2026. A three-time former congress mp from punjab, bittu was inducted as a minister of state in the narendra modi-led government in june 2024.

Article Title: SC agrees to hear PIL against police excesses on Monday
Article Text:
SC to hear PIL

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Friday agreed to hear Monday a PIL by an advocate for framing and scrupulous implementation of national guidelines ensuring "no police officer or security personnel shall carry out crowd control, public assembly management or arrests in plainclothes without displaying identity".CJI Surya Kant clarified that he was misquoted in the media when he refused to entertain another advocate who was highlighting the issues arising from the July 20 protest march and police action.In his plea, Shailendra Mani Tripathi sought an independent commission headed by a retired SC judge to inquire into the excessive force used against students and arbitrary detentions by Delhi Police during Monday's CJP's march to Parliament, and suspension and prosecution of all identified delinquent police officers.He urged SC to ban “rolling, repetitive, or blanket prohibitory orders in any area without an objectively verified, proximate and recorded threat of grave public disorder”.He also said the court must direct authorities not to prosecute any person for political dissent, academic critique, peaceful protest or criticism of govt unless there is a “direct, proximate, and imminent incitement to armed rebellion or secessionist violence”.The PIL, filed through advocate Chand Qureshi, sought a declaration that “any use of coercive force by unidentifiable or plainclothes personnel during public assemblies as arbitrary, illegal and a major service misconduct”.Referring to the earlier petition and his reported remarks, the CJI said, “He (petitioner) said he has filed a petition and sent a letter to SC. On inquiry, we found that neither the petition had been filed nor the letter had been sent. How can a court entertain a plea without a single paper before it?” the CJI asked.
Article Summary: Cji surya kant clarified that he was misquoted in the media when he refused to entertain another advocate. Shailendra mani tripathi sought an independent commission headed by a retired sc judge to inquire into the excessive force used against students and arbitrary detentions by delhi police.

Article Title: 'Have a heart': Sonam Wangchuk's wife slams critics after he ends 26-day hunger strike
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Gitanjali Angmo on Friday came to the defence of her husband Sonam Wangchuk 's decision to end his 26-day hunger strike against the NEET paper leak, urging critics to show compassion instead of rushing to judge him.In a post on X, Angmo said Wangchuk had "chosen sacrifice over comfort" and added that not everyone was qualified to judge a life dedicated to selfless service."Before you rush to criticise Sonam Wangchuk, first pause to earn the ethos of fasting for 26 days for a cause larger than yourself," Angmo said."He lies in the ICU today, having lost 11 kg, including muscle mass, because he chose sacrifice over comfort. The least we can offer him is a day of compassion before burdening him with our own expectations and political calculations. Not everyone is qualified to judge a life of selfless service. One must first earn the moral stature to do so. Please. Have a heart," she added.This comes after Wangchuk ended his hunger strike in the presence of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, saying the decision followed prolonged negotiations and was taken to avoid any possibility of violence in the country.In a separate post on X, Wangchuk said he broke his fast in the presence of the two Union ministers and senior leaders of the Apex Body of Leh Ladakh.He added that 65 MPs from different political parties had either visited him or signed letters urging him to end the fast.Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) said it would continue its nationwide "peaceful protests" demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak."The Cockroach Janata Party's peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar will continue until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns," CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said in a statement after Wangchuk ended his hunger strike.
Article Summary: Sonam wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike against the neet paper leak. His wife gitanjali angmo urged critics to show compassion instead of rushing to judge him. "not everyone is qualified to judge a life of selfless service," she said.

Article Title: After DU, JNU asks its students, staff to avoid Jantar Mantar protest site
Article Text:
The university has also asked to exercise responsibility on social media.

NEW DELHI: The Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) Friday asked its "all stakeholers" to "refrain from participating in or visiting gatherings at or around Jantar Mantar" that has been witnessing mobilisation against the perpetual exam paper leaks and the alleged irregularities in the education system.The university has also asked to "exercise responsibility" on social media as violations may "invite legal consequences under applicable laws as well as disciplinary action under the University’s code of conduct"."Advisory All stakeholders of JNU’s epistemic community are advised to act responsibly and prioritize their personal safety. In accordance with the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India’s directions on public demonstrations, you are requested to refrain from participating in or visiting gatherings at or around Jantar Mantar, New Delhi," the University posted on X.It futher wrote: "Please exercise responsibility on social media. Violations may invite legal consequences under applicable laws as well as disciplinary action under the University’s code of conduct. You are also encouraged to uphold the values of academic responsibility and responsible citizenship."Earlier, the University of Delhi (DU) has issued an official safety advisory, urging all students and faculty members to strictly refrain from participating in unauthorised assemblies and demonstrations at Jantar Mantar.The notification comes amid heightened concerns regarding student safety, legal consequences, and the rapid spread of misinformation surrounding recent events in the national capital.In a post on X, the university reminded students that demonstrations at Jantar Mantar are strictly regulated under the directives of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India. Participating in unlawful assemblies could lead to direct legal action by law enforcement authorities.Highlighting the broader ramifications of legal involvement, the administration warned that police action or legal records could severely compromise students' academic progress, campus standings, and future career opportunities.The administration flagged a surge in fake news, altered media, and misleading online content designed to provoke emotions and escalate tensions. Students have been advised to exercise extreme caution and verify information before reacting or sharing.Taking strong exception to Delhi University's notice, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi lashed out at the univerity for "threatening" the students for exercising the democratic rights."How dare you threaten students for exercising their democratic rights? Please note, you are the ones that will be held accountable when the time comes," Congress leader Rahul Gandh worte on X.
Article Summary: Jawaharlal nehru university (jnu) friday asked its "all stakeholers" to "refrain from participating in or visiting gatherings at or around jantar mantar" the university has also asked to "exercise responsibility" on social media as violations may "invite legal consequences under applicable laws"

Article Title: Police identify 2,500 people with criminal records at Jantar Mantar protest through facial recognition cameras
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Delhi police has identified more than 2,500 people with criminal backgrounds through Facial Recognition System deployed around the protest site at Jantar Mantar, news agency PTI reported, citing sources."The technology has so far helped identify over 2,500 persons with criminal antecedents. It acts as a strong deterrent and allows us to keep a close watch on those who may attempt to misuse the protest to create law and order problems," sources told PTI.According to the sources, the FRS units have been positioned at key entry and exit points around the protest site and are directly linked to the Delhi Police database."The objective is to ensure that people with criminal backgrounds do not exploit the protest to create law and order issues," sources told PTI."The system is connected with the Delhi Police database and can identify wanted criminals, absconders, history-sheeters, and Bad Characters (BCs) whose details already exist in police records," they added.According to an officer, the FRS does not target ordinary protesters but is meant to identify those with criminal antecedents who may attempt to take advantage of large gatherings."These are high-resolution cameras capable of capturing facial images even from a distance.Once a face is captured, it is quickly matched with the police database. If a wanted or absconding accused is detected, the concerned police unit is immediately alerted, and legal action can be initiated without delay," he said.Police said the technology will also help identify habitual offenders who have repeatedly figured in criminal cases and are listed as "Bad Characters" in Delhi Police records."The deployment acts as both a preventive and investigative tool. It helps us remain alert against anti-social elements who may try to infiltrate the protest, create a nuisance, or disturb law and order," another officer said.The installation of the FRS forms part of enhanced security arrangements around Jantar Mantar.
Article Summary: Delhi police has identified more than 2,500 people with criminal backgrounds. Facial recognition system deployed around the protest site at jantar mantar. Frs units have been positioned at key entry and exit points around protest site. "the objective is to ensure that people withcriminal backgrounds do not exploit the protest to create law and order issues," sources said.

Article Title: Dharmendra Pradhan must go to let Parl function: Oppn
Article Text:
Opposition has been demanding Pradhan's resignation

NEW DELHI: The Opposition rebuffed PM Modi's late-night video and proposed law on fast-track courts for paper leaks, as it reiterated that education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation is a must for restoring normalcy in Parliament. The aggressive stance has put a question mark on if introduction of the new bill Monday would bring the opposition bloc back to proceedings after a week of washout.The tone was set late last night when Rahul Gandhi reacted to Modi's statement, saying students are demanding Pradhan's exit and "don't insult their intelligence with this pathetic midnight video". The anti-BJP parties will meet Monday morning to take a final stand on the issue, but a flurry of statements from opposition netas suggested they are unlikely to relent. With CJP in talks with govt, there was some anxiety in the opposition camp about the stand it might take. A Congress neta said a drastic about-face would impact the decision of the political class too.
Article Summary: Opposition rebuffed pm modi's late-night video and proposed law on fast-track courts for paper leaks. Education minister dharmendra pradhan's resignation is a must for restoring normalcy in parliament. The aggressive stance has put a question mark on if introduction of the new bill monday would bring the opposition bloc back to proceedings after a week of washout.
